messages:
Maya Chen: heads up — ran into a reproducible issue in the new payments sampleapp where a 429 during token refresh caused duplicate POSTs to our webhook endpoint.
Samir Patel: ugh. do you have a minimal repro?
Maya Chen: yes. steps: run sampleapp with short token TTL (5s), hit it with two parallel requests, force a 429 from the auth service during refresh. sometimes both requests replay.
kevin_devex: is this the unsafe-replay on refresh we saw before or something new?
Maya Chen: variant. previous ones were around streaming resume; here it’s sync request path + immediate retry. The SDK's refresh flow replays the original request after refresh without replay-safety checks.
luke_infra: can we add a quick guard: attach transient-id header on outgoing requests and have the SDK refuse to replay if header present? e.g., X-Redwood-Transient-Id
Samir Patel: I proposed idempotency keys for paid endpoints but this is broader — some users won't set idempotency. A transient header + short-lived server-side dedupe would be lower friction.
Maya Chen: exact. PoC in node sdk:
```js
// pseudo
const tid = uuid();
req.headers['x-redwood-transient-id'] = tid;
if (auth.needsRefresh()) { await auth.refresh(); /* but only replay if the server says safe */ }
```
kevin_devex: worry: this adds a header on every request. opt-in? opt-out?
luke_infra: default on for SDKs, but servers can ignore. We should document and make it configurable: enableTransientReplayProtection: true.
Samir Patel: also need parity across languages — we had node/python differences before. Add acceptance tests in sampleapp harness that simulate refresh races.
Maya Chen: agreed. I can add a failing e2e to sampleapp that replicates 429-on-refresh. Would help CI catch regressions.
kevin_devex: what about jitter/backoff? If both clients retry immediately after refresh, they'd still double-post unless guard present. We should recommend randomized backoff + small jitter on replay attempts.
Samir Patel: +1. propose default backoff: exponential with base 100ms and jitter +- 50ms for client-initiated replays. Put server-side dedupe TTL = 5s for transient ids.
luke_infra: deploy-bot FYI: we should avoid changing prod behavior without rollout. maybe ship as opt-in flag in SDK and flip default after 2 weeks.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] canary rollout scheduled: devex sampleapp + 3 SDK integration tests at 2024-07-04T18:00Z.
Maya Chen: plan: I’ll open a PR to node SDK with transient header + jittered replay + test harness. Samir can mirror to python. Kevin please add an SDK config flag and docs snippet.
kevin_devex: will do. docs quick snippet:
```yaml
# SDK config
replayProtection:
  enabled: true
  backoff_base_ms: 100
  jitter_pct: 0.5
  transient_header: X-Redwood-Transient-Id
```
Samir Patel: also add note in onboarding guide: "If your backend is not idempotent, enable transient replay protection or configure server-side dedupe."
Maya Chen: filing action items: PR (node) -> #1729, PR (python) -> #1730, sampleapp e2e -> #1731. I'll paste links when up.
kevin_devex: can someone pair-review? I can take node if Maya wants.
Maya Chen: appreciated — I’ll ping when ready.
Samir Patel: thanks — this should cut down our dup charges and onboarding confusion.
kevin_devex: :thumbsup:
Maya Chen: one more micro-ask: add a small diag log when a replay is suppressed so devs can debug without enabling verbose traces. "replay suppressed transient-id=<id>"
luke_infra: fine. keep logs low volume.
Maya Chen: done, thanks everyone.
